raw_answer_text:
A1: The four messages are DHCPDISCOVER, DHCPOFFER, DHCPREQUEST, and DHCPACK, sent in that order; the DHCPDISCOVER is sent first by the client.
A2: A server sends both the DHCPOFFER and the DHCPACK.
A3: The arrival of the DHCPACK (yiaddr=192.0.2.44) moves the client into the BOUND state.
A4: The client moves into the RENEWING state, and it sends the DHCPREQUEST as a unicast to server B, the server that holds the binding.
A5: The client moves into the REBINDING state, and instead of unicasting to the binding server it broadcasts the DHCPREQUEST so that any server (here server A and server B) may respond.
A6: NOT STATED.
A7: DHCPRELEASE is used to give up the lease (causing the server to discard the lease, per the description referencing Figure 3), and it is sent by the client.
A8: The client broadcasts a DHCPREQUEST naming server-id=B, and any server whose offer was not named in that DHCPREQUEST (here server A) reads it as a declined offer and may return its offered address to its pool.
